title: Module and local Hom transport under a ringed-topos equivalence
statement: Let $e:(\mathscr X,R)\to(\mathscr X',R')$ be an equivalence of ringed topoi presented by small sites, where $R,R'$ are sheaves of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]: its underlying geometric morphism is an equivalence and $e^{-1}R'\to R$ is an isomorphism. The module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] is an exact equivalence $e^*\dashv e_*$ of module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Termwise application gives mutually inverse equivalences of unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], preserving K-injective complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For every sheaf of sets $V'$ in $\mathscr X'$, the induced equivalence on the slice topoi [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction] over $V'$ and $e^{-1}V'$ has these same properties for the restricted rings. Slice over a site object means slice over its sheafified representable [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable]. These equivalences commute with further restrictions, derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and localization of the restricted ring at a section [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. For every $N\in D(R')$ and every ideal subsheaf $\mathcal I'\subset R'$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-ideal-generators], put $\mathcal I=e^*\mathcal I'$. Then the tests $R\mathcal Hom(R'|_{V'}[1/a],N|_{V'})=0$ for all site objects $V'$ and $a\in\mathcal I'(V')$ hold if and only if the tests $R\mathcal Hom(R|_V[1/b],e^*N|_V)=0$ hold for all site objects $V$ of the other presentation and $b\in\mathcal I(V)$.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-equivalence-module-hom] for the module equivalence, its specified underlying comparison, regular-unit map and two derived internal-Hom comparisons. Equivalences preserve binary products and zero maps, so they are additive; they preserve all limits and colimits. The exact-inverse adjunction preserves K-injectives. Apply exact-functor localization for the termwise factorization and the derived unit and counit. The inverse regular-unit map is the inverse image of the forward map followed by the inverse module-equivalence unit. The inverse derived Hom comparison is obtained from the forward one by cancelling the equivalence on the output and its opposite-product equivalence on the inputs.

A natural regular-unit isomorphism commuting with scalars gives an isomorphism of the two constant-object sequential diagrams by NatTrans.ofSequence. Compare their colimit cocones after applying the colimit-preserving functor. The stage-zero equation of [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-regular-colimit] gives exactly the localization unit equation. This constructs the localization field for every equivalence and restriction core.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-element-restriction-hom] to both rings and complete its cores using the preceding sequential-colimit argument. Derive their termwise comparisons and relocalization in the derived categories by mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso. The actual restriction additivity, exactness, K-injective preservation, element-map continuity and relocalization are supplied by the five proved APIs of RingedPresentationData. The restriction lemma supplies only its nonformal Hom and further-restriction/site-object comparisons.

Choose the actual element-site slice adjunctions from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-equivalence-slices] to construct the slice ringed morphisms with their set and structural comparisons and module squares. Complete each slice module equivalence as in step 1. Apply the functorial derived composition isomorphisms to the module squares to obtain the two derived squares.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-equivalence-local-tests] for every unbounded N and every monomorphism of the ideal into the regular module. Assemble these fields into the original unchanged RingedPresentationTransport record.

theorem ringed_presentation_transport
    {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} {S : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{u}}
    (e : RingedToposMorphism (localCoefficientRings R) (localCoefficientRings S))
    [e.inverse.IsEquivalence] [IsIso e.ringMap] :
    Nonempty (RingedPresentationTransport e)
